images.caption:
The old gun emplacement at Fjell Festning (Fjell Fortress), as it appeared in mid 2004. The gun was the B-tower from the German battleship Gneisenau. The steel plating lying in front in the picture, is armour from the now removed gun turret. 

The emplacement has later been modified, and a large glass housing has been placed on top of it. This was mainly to prevent rain entering the main tunnel system, but the building also contains a café. On the outside, the grass was removed (and the gunpost for a while looked as it did when the gun was operational), rain coating was applied, but dirt has now been put back on the concrete, a road (not original) has been constructed and a building containing toilets has been built close to the gun emplacement.

images.caption:
A "Panzersperre" from WWII: eight large rocks placed on top of a concrete base, as it stands on sides of the road leading up to "Batterie Fjell", at Sotra island, Hordaland - Norway. Originally, the rocks were held in place by a thick wire only, which could be cut in case should enemy troops land and try to advance towards the Fjell Fortress via the road. The eight heavy rocks would, when the wire was cut, fall down on the road and block the way for tanks and cars. On the right hand side, there is a steep hill impossible to climb for tracked or wheeled vehicles, to the left there is a wetland, bog, also impossible to cross. 
This particular roadblock is a rare construction: a german standard roadblock was named "Walzkörpersperre", and was made entirely of concrete. 

See also a closeup: Image:Panzersperre batterie fjell closeup.JPG

images.caption:
What remains of the Prisoner of War camp at Horebotn, Sotra island, Norway. This might be a chimney, but is more likely a corner or a support for one of the barracks that was built here. 

This was a camp built temporarily to house prisoners (mainly people from eastern Europe) that was forced to build the road leading up to and the "Fjell Fortress" itself. Later, a larger camp was built in a different pace.

images.caption:
Dies ist eine Zeichnung der "Magnet umlader" (Magnetische reloademaschine) für den Deutschen 28 cm Schiffskanone C/34 Pistole. Die C/34 Gewehre in der dhr platziert wurden. C/28 Geschützturm, ursprünglich auf den Schiffen "Scharnhorst" und "Gneisenau". "Gneisenau" wurde in einem Luftangriff 1942 beschädigt, und ihre Waffen wurden an Land gestellt wird, in rippenbögen Batterien. Zwei der Türme, mit insgesamt sechs Gewehren, wurden in Norwegen gestellt wird, in das Fort Austrått und Fjell, von denen die eine an das Fort Austrått bleibt nach wie vor als ein Museum heute. Der dritte Turm wurde in Holland gelegt. Datum unbekannt. Krupp. 52 Sk c 34 Magnet umlader
Die Bildunterschriften werden von unseren Anbietern zur Verfügung gestellt.

images.caption: This is a drawing of the commando bunker at Fjell Festning, Hordaland, Norway. The bunker, a S446 Leitstand, was home for a large direction and rangefinder, meant to direct costal artillery.
images.alt: This is a drawing of the commando bunker at Fjell Festning, Hordaland, Norway. The bunker, a S446 Leitstand, was home for a large direction and rangefinder, meant to direct costal artillery.

images.caption: A view from Fjell Festning, showing, in front, a M19-bunker, (known as R633), and in the background a S446 can be seen (with the black "stub" on top). The S446 was a commando bunker, on which was placed a range- and directionfinder. This particular bunker was used after the war by the Norwegian Navy, as a radar station, so the black "stub" is not original, this was where the radar was placed until 2005.
